course: Pizza Oven Construction - Wood Fired 12 Pizza

lessons.title: Installing a Gas Assist or Hybrid Burner
lessons.body: A gas assist burner lets you start your wood-fired oven quickly without waiting for kindling to catch, and it helps maintain temperature when your wood is damp or when you need consistent heat for multiple pizzas. For a 12-pizza oven, you need a burner rated at least 15,000 BTU (4.4 kW). In many African cities, LPG is widely available, so a propane burner is practical. First, check local regulationsâsome areas require a licensed technician for gas connections. Gather tools: adjustable wrench, pipe thread sealant (gas-rated), soapy water for leak testing, and a drill with a 25mm hole saw. Choose a burner designed for outdoor ovens, with a safety shut-off valve. Position the burner at the back or side of the oven floor, about 10 cm above the floor, aimed toward the center. Drill a hole through the oven wall or base for the gas pipe. Use black iron pipe or copper tubing, never standard garden hose. Connect the burner to the pipe, then to a regulator and gas cylinder. Apply sealant to all threaded joints. Turn on the gas and brush soapy water on every jointâbubbles mean a leak. Tighten or re-tape until no bubbles appear. Test the burner: open the gas valve slightly and ignite with a long lighter. Adjust the air shutter on the burner until the flame is blue with a slight roar. A yellow flame means too little air. Once working, secure the pipe with clamps and cover any gaps with fire cement. Always keep a fire extinguisher nearby and never leave the gas on unattended. With a gas assist, you can preheat the oven to 400Â°C in 20 minutes instead of 1 hour, saving time and wood.

lessons.title: Adding a Built-in Thermometer
lessons.body: A built-in thermometer takes the guesswork out of baking. For a wood-fired pizza oven, you need a thermometer that reads up to 500Â°C. Dial thermometers with a 5 cm probe are cheap and common in hardware stores. Digital thermometers with a probe and wire are more accurate but require a battery. Start by drilling a 10 mm hole through the oven dome, about 15 cm above the floor and 10 cm from the front. The hole should go through the brick or refractory concrete. Insert the probe so it sits inside the oven, not touching the wall. For a dial thermometer, the stem should be at least 10 cm long. Secure it with fire cement or a metal bracket. For a digital probe, feed the wire through the hole and seal with high-temperature silicone. Mount the display unit on the oven stand or wall. Test the thermometer by heating the oven slowly. Compare its reading with an infrared gun aimed at the floor. If they differ by more than 20Â°C, adjust the probe depth. Many learners in Africa use a simple oven thermometer placed on the floor, but a built-in one lets you monitor without opening the door. This is crucial for bread baking, where you need steady 220Â°C. For pizza, you want 350â450Â°C. A built-in thermometer helps you learn your oven's personality: where hot spots are, how quickly it loses heat. Clean the probe occasionally with a wire brush. If the dial fogs up, it's not sealed for high heatâreplace it with a better model. A good thermometer costs about $10â20 and lasts years.

lessons.title: Designing a Wood Storage Area
lessons.body: Dry wood is essential for a clean, hot fire. A wood storage area keeps your fuel dry and organized. For a 12-pizza oven, you need space for at least 0.5 cubic meters of woodâenough for 3â4 baking sessions. Build the storage under the oven, beside it, or on a separate rack. Under-oven storage is convenient: the oven stand often has empty space. But make sure the wood is at least 30 cm below the oven floor to avoid overheating. Use a metal or concrete shelf. If building beside the oven, create a simple rack from metal angle iron or treated timber. A roof is essentialârain ruins wood. Use corrugated iron or plastic sheet. Leave the sides open for airflow. Stack wood loosely so air can circulate. Keep wood off the ground on a pallet or bricks to prevent termites and moisture. In humid regions, add a small vent or use a mesh back. For kindling, keep a separate bin with small sticks, cardboard, and dry leaves. Never store wood against the oven's hot exteriorâkeep a 10 cm gap. If you have limited space, a vertical rack on wheels lets you move it. A good wood storage area also improves safety: no tripping over logs. Teach your customers or family to take wood from the bottom of the stack first, so older wood gets used. Replace stock regularly. In many African markets, you can buy wood by the bundle; store it immediately under cover. A simple 1m x 1m x 1m rack holds about 0.7 cubic meters. Build it from 50mm angle iron welded or bolted together. Cost: about $30â50.

lessons.title: Creating a Multi-Purpose Oven (Bread, Roasts)
lessons.body: Your pizza oven can do much more than pizza. After the pizza session, when the temperature drops to 250Â°C, you can bake bread. At 180â200Â°C, roast meat, vegetables, or casseroles. The key is managing heat. After pizzas, close the oven door and let the fire die down. Wait until the thermometer reads 220Â°C for bread. For crusty loaves, you need steam: throw a cup of water on the hot floor and quickly close the door. For roasts, use a cast iron pot or baking tray. Place meat on a rack so it doesn't stew in fat. A 2 kg chicken takes about 1 hour at 180Â°C. For slow-cooked stews, bring the oven to 150Â°C, then put in a covered pot and leave for 3â4 hours. The residual heat works like a slow cooker. To bake bread, shape dough into rounds, slash the top, and slide onto the floor with a peel. Bake for 25â30 minutes. You can also bake flatbreads, injera, or chapati directly on the floor. For multiple batches, you may need to add a small stick of wood to maintain temperature. A multi-purpose oven increases your income: you can sell bread in the morning, pizza at night, and roast on weekends. Clean the floor between different foods with a wire brush. Never use soap. If you roast fish, the smell may lingerâair out the oven before baking bread. With practice, you'll learn your oven's temperature curve: it drops about 50Â°C per hour with the door closed. Plan your baking accordingly. This versatility makes your oven a true community asset.

lessons.title: Building a Prep Counter and Sink
lessons.body: A prep counter next to your oven speeds up pizza making. You need a sturdy surface at waist height (about 90 cm) for stretching dough, topping pizzas, and cutting. Build it from concrete, wood, or metal. A simple frame from 50mm square tubing, topped with a 5 cm thick concrete slab or hardwood planks, works well. Make the counter at least 60 cm deep and 1.2 m long. If space allows, add a lower shelf for flour bins and tools. For hygiene, a sink is essential. You can install a simple hand-wash sink with a 20-liter jerrycan and a tap, or a proper plumbed sink if you have water supply. A plastic basin set into the counter works too. Place the sink within arm's reach of the prep area. Use a bucket underneath to catch wastewater, or connect to a drain. Keep a bucket of clean water and soap for handwashing. In many African settings, a tippy-tap is a cheap alternative: a jerrycan with a string-operated tap. But for a commercial setup, a small stainless steel sink is best. Mount it at the end of the counter. Add a drying rack. Also consider a waste bin for scrapsâkeep it covered. Cover the counter with food-grade sealant if using wood. Concrete should be sealed with a food-safe epoxy. Clean the counter after every use. A good prep counter reduces accidents and improves speed. You can build the whole unit for under $100 using local materials. Remember to leave space for a flour bin, a topping tray, and a pizza peel. This station turns your oven into a professional workspace.

lessons.title: Lighting and Electrical Considerations
lessons.body: Good lighting lets you work safely after dark and attracts customers. For a wood-fired oven, use LED floodlights (10â20W) mounted on a pole or wall, aimed at the oven mouth and prep area. Avoid halogenâthey get hot and attract insects. If you have grid electricity, run a weatherproof cable (2.5mmÂ²) from your main board to a junction box near the oven. Install an RCD (residual current device) for safety. Use IP65 rated fittings outdoors. If no grid, use a solar panel with a battery: a 50W panel and a 12V 100Ah battery can power lights and a small fridge. For the oven itself, you may need electricity for a gas assist ignition (if electronic) or a thermometer display. Keep cables away from hot surfacesâuse metal conduit. Never run cables over the oven dome. For ambiance, string lights or a small spotlight on the chimney can be attractive. Also consider a small exhaust fan if you build the oven indoorsâbut wood-fired ovens should be outdoors or in a well-ventilated shed. If you install a rotisserie motor, use a heat-resistant cable. All electrical work must be done by a qualified person if you are not confident. In many African countries, you can hire an electrician for $20â50. Test your RCD monthly. Keep a torch (flashlight) handy for power cuts. Solar lights are a good backup. Finally, label your breakers clearly: 'Oven Lights', 'Sink Pump', etc. This makes troubleshooting easy. Proper lighting and safe wiring turn your oven into a reliable business asset.

lessons.title: Practical Reference
lessons.body:
Practical Reference: Advanced Oven Features and Accessories

This module is written for the African pizza entrepreneur who already has a working wood-fired oven and now wants to raise output, cut fuel waste, and add revenue streams. In most African markets â Lagos, Nairobi, Accra, Kampala, Kigali â the pizza business competes on consistency and speed as much as on taste. A 12-inch pizza oven that only bakes pizza is a single-product asset. The same oven, fitted with a gas assist burner, a built-in thermometer, a wood store, and a prep counter, becomes a multi-product kitchen: pizza by night, bread and roasts by day, catering orders on weekends.

This lesson is a practical reference. It covers installation logic, cost-benefit, sourcing realities, and the safety rules that protect your investment. Treat every accessory as a business decision: what does it add to throughput, margin, or product range, and what does it cost in cash, fuel, and maintenance?

1. Installing a Gas Assist or Hybrid Burner

A gas assist burner (LPG) sits beside or under the wood fire and provides instant, controllable heat. In African operations this solves three problems: slow morning start-up, inconsistent heat during rainy season when wood is damp, and the labour cost of one person feeding wood continuously.

Business case: A hybrid oven can reach 350â400Â°C in 20â25 minutes instead of 60â90 minutes on wood alone. That is roughly 40 extra minutes of selling time per day. If your average pizza sells for the equivalent of US$6 and you bake 15 more pizzas in that window, the burner pays for itself within weeks.

Installation practicalities: Use a certified LPG regulator and hose rated for high-temperature zones. Keep the burner at least 150 mm from the oven mouth and shield it from ash and grease. Fit a shut-off valve outside the oven footprint so you can isolate gas instantly. In markets where LPG cylinders are refilled informally, insist on a soap-bubble leak test at every cylinder change.

Cost note: Gas is often cheaper per hour than charcoal or hardwood in urban African markets, but prices vary. Track your cost per pizza on wood-only versus hybrid for two weeks before committing to a permanent change.

2. Adding a Built-in Thermometer

Most oven failures are temperature failures â too cold, the base is soggy; too hot, the crust burns before the cheese melts. A built-in thermometer (analogue dial or digital probe) gives you repeatability, which is the foundation of a franchise-ready brand.

Install the probe at dome height, not on the floor, because floor and dome temperatures differ by 50â100Â°C. For a 12-inch oven, the ideal baking floor temperature is 350â430Â°C, with the dome slightly hotter for top colour. A digital infrared thermometer is a useful backup for checking the floor before each bake.

3. Designing a Wood Storage Area

Wood is your fuel inventory. In many African cities, dry hardwood is seasonal and price-volatile, so storage is a financial strategy, not just a convenience. Build a raised, ventilated wood store beside the oven â never directly under the baking floor unless the structure is fire-rated and insulated.

Raise wood at least 100 mm off the ground to prevent termites and damp. Cover the top, leave the sides open for airflow. Buy in bulk during the dry season when prices are lowest, and season wood for at least 6â12 months. Wet wood wastes 30â50% of its energy boiling off moisture.

4. Creating a Multi-Purpose Oven (Bread, Roasts)

After the pizza lunch and dinner rush, the oven retains heat for hours. Use that residual heat for bread, roasts, and catering. This is the single biggest margin opportunity in the module.

Bread: Bake sourdough or local flatbreads in the 220â260Â°C falling-temperature window. Roasts: Whole chicken, goat, or vegetables at 180â200Â°C using the retained heat after the fire dies down. Catering: Sell "oven-roasted" platters to offices and events, using the same fuel you already paid for.

5. Building a Prep Counter and Sink

Health inspectors and corporate clients both look for a clean, separate prep area. A stainless-steel or tiled counter beside the oven, with a small sink and hand-wash station, reduces cross-contamination and speeds up service. In many African municipalities, a hand-wash basin is a licensing requirement for food premises.

Design the counter at 900 mm height, with under-counter storage for flour, sauce, and boxes. Position it within one step of the oven mouth so the pizza maker never turns their back on the bake.

6. Lighting and Electrical Considerations

Evening trade is where pizza margins are highest, so lighting is revenue infrastructure. Use LED work lights over the prep counter and a warm light at the oven mouth so staff can see crust colour. If you run a gas assist, dough mixer, fridge, or POS system, you need a stable power supply â consider an inverter or small solar backup in areas with load-shedding.

â  SAFETY WARNING â GAS AND FIRE

LPG is heavier than air and pools in low areas. Never install a gas cylinder inside an enclosed oven base or below the baking floor. Always store cylinders upright, outdoors or in a ventilated cage, away from heat and direct sun. Check hoses and regulators for cracks every month, and replace any hose showing wear. Keep a dry-powder fire extinguisher within 3 metres of the oven and train every staff member to use it. In case of a gas smell: shut the valve, do not switch anything on or off, ventilate, and leave the area.

Quick Reference Checklist

  • â Gas assist burner installed with certified regulator, high-temp hose, and external shut-off valve.
  • â Built-in thermometer mounted at dome height; infrared thermometer used to verify floor temperature daily.
  • â Wood store raised 100 mm off ground, ventilated, covered, and stocked with seasoned wood bought in the dry season.
  • â Multi-product menu tested: at least one bread and one roast item using residual heat.
  • â Prep counter and hand-wash sink positioned within one step of the oven mouth.
  • â LED work lighting installed over prep area and oven mouth for evening service.
  • â Dry-powder fire extinguisher within 3 metres; all staff trained on gas leak response.
  • â Monthly leak test and hose inspection logged in a maintenance book.

Further Reading

  • FAO â Energy Programme (wood energy and sustainable biomass guidance)
  • IEA â Africa Energy Outlook 2022 (fuel access and pricing context)
  • HETAS â Solid Fuel and Biomass Appliance Safety (UK, widely referenced installation standard)
  • WHO â Air Quality and Health (indoor smoke and ventilation guidance)
  • ILO â Occupational Safety and Health (workplace safety for food businesses)

Bottom line for African pizza businesses: the oven is not just a cooking tool â it is a production asset. Gas assist buys you time, a thermometer buys you consistency, wood storage buys you price stability, and multi-product use buys you all-day revenue from one fire. Build the accessories into your capital plan from day one, and your 12-inch oven will out-earn a larger single-purpose oven every week.

quiz.q: What is the minimum BTU rating recommended for a gas assist burner on a 12-pizza oven?
quiz.explanation: A 15,000 BTU burner provides enough heat to assist a 12-pizza oven effectively.

quiz.q: Which type of pipe should be used for a gas connection to an oven burner?
options: B) Black iron pipe or copper tubing
quiz.explanation: Black iron or copper tubing is rated for gas and high temperatures, unlike garden hose or PVC.

quiz.q: How do you check for gas leaks after connecting a burner?
options: B) Light a match near joints
C) Brush soapy water on joints
quiz.explanation: Soapy water bubbles indicate a leak; never use a flame to test.

quiz.q: What color should the flame be on a properly adjusted gas burner?
options: B) Blue with a slight roar
quiz.explanation: A blue flame indicates complete combustion and proper air mixture.

quiz.q: Where should the gas burner be positioned inside the oven?
options: C) At the back or side, 10 cm above floor
quiz.explanation: Placing it at the back or side, 10 cm above the floor, aims heat toward the center.

quiz.q: What is the maximum temperature a built-in thermometer for a wood-fired oven should read?
quiz.explanation: Wood-fired ovens can reach 500Â°C, so the thermometer must handle that range.

quiz.q: Where should the probe of a built-in thermometer be placed?
options: B) Inside the oven, 15 cm above floor
quiz.explanation: The probe should be inside the dome, about 15 cm above the floor, to read baking temperature.

quiz.q: How can you seal the hole for a digital thermometer probe?
quiz.explanation: High-temperature silicone withstands oven heat and seals the hole.

quiz.q: What is a good temperature for baking bread in a wood-fired oven?
quiz.explanation: Bread bakes best around 220Â°C, after the oven has cooled from pizza temperatures.

quiz.q: Why should you compare a built-in thermometer with an infrared gun?
quiz.explanation: Comparing readings helps ensure the built-in thermometer is accurate.

quiz.q: How much wood storage space is recommended for a 12-pizza oven?
quiz.explanation: 0.5 cubic meters holds enough wood for several baking sessions.

quiz.q: Where should wood be stored relative to the oven?
options: A) Directly on top of the oven
B) At least 30 cm below the oven floor
quiz.explanation: Keeping wood at least 30 cm below the floor prevents overheating and fire risk.

quiz.q: What is essential for a wood storage area?
quiz.explanation: A roof keeps rain off and keeps wood dry.

quiz.q: Why should wood be stacked loosely?
quiz.explanation: Airflow helps wood dry and prevents mold.

quiz.q: What should you keep separate from main wood?
quiz.explanation: Kindling (small sticks, cardboard) is used for starting fires and should be kept dry and separate.

quiz.q: At what temperature can you bake bread after pizzas?
quiz.explanation: Bread is best baked around 220Â°C as the oven cools.

quiz.q: How do you create steam for crusty bread?
options: B) Throw water on the hot floor
quiz.explanation: Throwing water on the floor creates steam, which helps form a crust.

quiz.q: What temperature is good for slow-cooking a stew?
quiz.explanation: 150Â°C allows slow cooking using residual heat.

quiz.q: How long does a 2 kg chicken take to roast at 180Â°C?
quiz.explanation: A 2 kg chicken roasts in about 1 hour at 180Â°C.

quiz.q: What should you do between baking different foods?
quiz.explanation: A wire brush cleans the floor without soap, which can leave residue.

quiz.q: What is a good height for a prep counter?
quiz.explanation: 90 cm is a comfortable waist height for most people.

quiz.q: What material is best for a prep counter surface?
quiz.explanation: Concrete or hardwood are durable and can be sealed for food safety.

quiz.q: Why is a sink important near the oven?
options: A) For washing hands and tools
quiz.explanation: A sink allows handwashing and cleaning, which is essential for hygiene.

quiz.q: What is a tippy-tap?
options: B) A jerrycan with string-operated tap
quiz.explanation: A tippy-tap is a simple handwashing device using a jerrycan and string.

quiz.q: How should you seal a concrete prep counter?
quiz.explanation: Food-safe epoxy seals concrete and makes it easy to clean.

quiz.q: What type of lighting is recommended for an outdoor oven area?
quiz.explanation: LED floodlights are energy-efficient and don't attract insects as much as halogen.

quiz.q: What safety device should be installed on electrical circuits near an oven?
quiz.explanation: An RCD (residual current device) protects against electric shock.

quiz.q: What IP rating is needed for outdoor electrical fittings?
quiz.explanation: IP65 is weatherproof and suitable for outdoor use.

quiz.q: If using solar power, what size battery is suggested for lights and a small fridge?
quiz.explanation: A 12V 100Ah battery can power lights and a small fridge for a day.

quiz.q: Why should cables be kept away from the oven dome?
quiz.explanation: High heat can melt insulation and cause fires.
